PARIS — Pan-European missile maker MBDA and German startup Atmos Space Cargo are teaming up to study deploying deep-strike weapons from Earth orbit using reentry vehicles.
The firms agreed to jointly assess the feasibility and pursue development of a precision orbital deep strike capability, combining military payloads with orbital transport and reentry vehicles, they said on Wednesday. The cooperation agreement will initially focus on system architecture, technical feasibility, payload integration and possible technology demonstrations, MBDA and Atmos said.
Atmos CEO Sebastian Klaus has argued Europe needs an orbital deterrent to fill a capability gap in deep precision strike. He made the case in March for a conventional capability that can be deployed from orbit to strike any legitimate military target anywhere on Earth within 60 minutes.
“The agreement brings together our expertise in orbital transportation and atmospheric reentry with MBDA’s defense systems expertise to explore a potential new conventional defense capability,” Klaus said in a post on social network LinkedIn on Wednesday. “Our objective is clear: deterrence. To help European allies prevent aggression by strengthening the credibility of Europe’s ability to defend itself.”
The companies are assessing how existing defense technology and new orbital technology can be combined to strengthen Europe’s conventional deterrence, Klaus said in a statement on Wednesday, calling orbital transportation and return “a new layer of strategic infrastructure.”
Any future deployment and use would be subject to applicable law and decisions by the responsible governmental and military authorities, the startup said. Specific developments and future projects remain subject to further evaluation and separate agreements, according to Atmos.
Atmos will contribute expertise in orbital transportation and reentry technology, with MBDA providing capabilities in defense systems and military payloads, the companies said. MBDA, which is owned by Airbus, BAE Systems and Leonardo, is Europe’s largest missile maker.
“Our goal is to provide our armed forces with a highly innovative, sovereign European capability,” Thomas Gottschild, the managing director of MBDA Deutschland, said in a statement . “We are very much looking forward to this new project.”
Atmos is developing a reusable spacecraft for low-Earth orbit cargo missions that uses an inflatable cushion as a heat shield and aerodynamic brake for reentry. The startup successfully tested the concept in April 2025, and is developing the Phoenix 2 orbiter with a payload capacity of 100 kilograms. The company said flight duration can range from 3 hours to 12 months.
Atmos said its civilian Phoenix vehicles remain separate from the dedicated defense system being explored with MBDA.
The startup and the European Space Agency are also studying a larger version dubbed Phoenix 3 with a potential payload of about 1 metric ton.
Atmos in April this year raised €25.7 million in a Series A funding round that it said would help finance an initial three-vehicle fleet of Phoenix 2 spacecraft as well as development of Phoenix 3. The firm also said it was setting up a business serving government and defense customers called Atmos Works.
The company last year set up an alliance with ARX Robotics to integrate unmanned systems with its reentry vehicle, envisaging using Phoenix to deliver autonomous systems to the Earth’s surface, including to support defense operations on the ground.

Elon Musk says Tesla plans to build a version of the Model Y with no steering wheel and no pedals, a driverless people-mover he describes as “good for transporting groups of 6 or 7 people.”
It’s yet another vehicle nobody asked for, from a company that ended Model S and Model X production this year and is about to end the Cybertruck. And the data says very few car buyers want a car they can’t drive.
What Musk said
Musk made the comments on stage at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.
He pitched it as the answer to the Cybercab only carrying two people. “We still need autonomous vehicles if you’ve got 4 or 6, or a whole family,” Musk said, before adding that Tesla plans “an autonomous version of the Model Y that won’t have steering wheels or pedals.”

There was no timeline, no price and no word on where it would be built.
Six or seven seats points straight at the Model Y L, the stretched three-row Model Y that Tesla launched in the US in July for $61,990 , or the regular Model Y with the $2,500 seven-seat option Tesla brought back in January.
The Model Y L wasn’t supposed to need to exist
Here’s the funny part. When Tesla launched the Model Y L in China in August 2025, Musk said it might never come to the US , “given the advent of self-driving in America.”
The idea was that autonomy would make a bigger family car pointless. Less than a year later, Tesla was building the Model Y L at Giga Texas and selling it at the top of the Model Y lineup.
Now Musk wants a driverless version of that same car. So families still need a big vehicle, self-driving or not. That’s what we said in 2025.
Tesla’s Model Y robotaxis already have a steering wheel
The robotaxi argument doesn’t hold up either. Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet is mostly Model Ys, and those cars have a steering wheel and pedals.
The wheel isn’t what’s stopping them from driving themselves. Removing it mostly makes the car useless outside Tesla’s geofences.
We’ve already seen what that looks like. Tesla opened personal Cybercab orders last week at $29,990, but the car only works inside Robotaxi service areas and requires a $299 per month subscription to operate at all.
There’s also the regulatory mess. Tesla self-certified the Cybercab as compliant with federal safety standards even though FMVSS 135 calls for a foot-operated service brake, and NHTSA responded with a Special Order in September. Zoox took the slower route and got a Part 555 exemption, which caps it at 2,500 vehicles a year. A second vehicle with no controls means a second round of that fight.
Buyers don’t want cars without controls
Cox Automotive’s 2026 Autonomous Vehicle Study asked US consumers which level of autonomy they’d find most appealing in a vehicle they own. Only 10% picked fully driverless Level 5, down from 17% when Cox first asked in 2016.
The most popular choice was Level 4 at 28%: full autonomy, but with the option for a human to drive. And only 38% said they’d feel safe in a Level 5 vehicle, compared to 87% for a modern car with basic driver aids.
So after a decade of exposure to self-driving tech, interest in a car with no controls went down, not up.
Electrek’s Take
Tesla already makes the Model Y. It already makes a six-seat Model Y. Just make the Model Y.
In 2016, Musk’s Master Plan Part Deux promised to “expand the electric vehicle product line to address all major segments.” Ten years later, once the Cybertruck ends next summer, Tesla’s consumer lineup is the Model 3 and Model Y. That’s it. No affordable car (Musk called a non-robotaxi $25,000 Tesla “pointless” in 2024), no compact crossover, no minivan, no midsize pickup.

This seems pretty obvious as something needed for their Robotaxi service. It lets you move 6 people, including the driver's seat.
I of course remain skeptical that Tesla is going to scale up their Level 4/5 self-driving to end consumers in unconstrained geography anytime soon, but they do have a service that drives people around in specific areas with no driver, and a larger vehicle for that service is necessary when their primary vehicle only holds 2 passengers.

Every time there’s a gap in Tesla’s lineup, Musk gives the same answer: autonomy will fill it. The Model Y L was going to be unnecessary. The cheap car was pointless. The Model S and X made way for Optimus, and the Cybertruck for the Cybercab.
But Tesla’s own robotaxi fleet proves you don’t need to remove the steering wheel to run a robotaxi. Keeping it costs Tesla almost nothing and keeps the car useful for the roughly 90% of buyers who still want the option to drive. Taking it out only adds a federal compliance fight and shrinks the market to people who live inside a geofence.

All 2026 Formula 1 Drivers Can Now Be Had as LEGO Minifigures for the First Time, Race Cars in Tow
15 photos
Photo: LEGO
It's been two years since the organizers of one of the most intense racing series on the planet, Formula 1, and Danish toy maker LEGO tied the knot, and the gift keeps on giving. Taking advantage of the Las Vegas Grand Prix scheduled for this coming weekend, the partners announced the arrival of something that has never been offered in LEGO form on this scale before.
That would be LEGO minifigure versions of all 22 drivers that have lined up on the starting grid this season, complete with detailed printed helmets and race suits and even their respective names and driver numbers.
Accompanying these plastic drivers are the remade versions of all the 11 cars that have competed this season. They have been updated to mimic this season's regulations and liveries, and they are, just like before, part of the Speed Champions series.
LEGO says the new sets replicating the 2026 F1 season cars and drivers will become available on March 1, 2027, which kind of makes them a little late to the party – as a reminder, the competition's next season kicks off on the weekend of March 12.
Photo: LEGO Even so, here they all are, complete with details about the number of parts and LEGO's internal code. As a side note, all cars are priced on the American market at $29.99, and they can already be pre-ordered by those interested. All cars are sized at 1.5 inches (4 cm) high, 2.5 inches (6 cm) wide, and 7.5 inches (19 cm) long once fully assembled.
LEGO Speed Champions McLaren Mastercard MCL40 F1 Race Car (77269) - 196 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS W17 F1 Race Car (77270) - 216 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 F1 Race Car (77268) - 203 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Scuderia Ferrari HP SF-26 F1 Race Car (77267) - 230 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Atlassian Williams FW48 F1 Race Car (77272) - 231 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Visa Cash App RB VCARB 03 F1 Race Car (77273) - 206 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Aston Martin Aramco AMR26 F1 Race Car (77271) - 199 pieces LEGO Speed Champions TGR Haas VF-26 F1 Race Car (77275) - 209 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Audi Revolut R26 F1 Race Car (77276) - 215 pieces LEGO Speed Champions BWT Alpine A526 F1 Race Car (77274) - 212 pieces LEGO Speed Champions Cadillac MAC-26 F1 Race Car (77277) - 212 pieces When revealing these new sets, LEGO said they are only the beginning of what's to come over the next few months from the partnership with Formula 1 . We'll keep an eye on that and report back once we learn more about it.
Separately, the coming Las Vegas F1 race will be packed with other LEGO things. The minicars the toy maker debuted at the British Grand Prix back in July will be on location, and they carry an undisclosed number of special modifications.
They will be part of the F1 weekend as they'll race with a playful twist, as the toy maker says, referring to who is going to drive them. The identity of the drivers will be made public on LEGO's social media channels in the coming hours.
Photo: LEGO The LEGO Race, as it's called, takes place on Saturday, November 21, when it will hit the Strip with 11 replicas of each of this season's real-world racers, which will complete a lap of the circuit for fun.
LEGO will also be present on the Las Vegas Monorail, where it will deploy a wrapped train along with a station domination at the Flamingo/Caesars Palace station.
It may very well happen that LEGO's presence in Las Vegas will be a tad more exciting than the race itself. I mean, who wouldn't want to see F1 cars race on the Las Vegas streets, but there's really no stake as play, if you really think about it.
Both the season's titles, Drivers' Championship and Constructors' Championship, have already been decided, and with three legs to go, mind you. This season's best driver is Mercedes' Andrea Kimi Antonelli , and the same German carmaker beat Ferrari and Red Bull Racing to the teams’ win.
There are, of course, a lot of points left in the competition, and that may impact the final standings below first place, but the fight for the win is over.
Photo: LEGO Following the Las Vegas race, Formula 1 is heading to Qatar on the last weekend of this month, and the weekend after that to Abu Dhabi for the final leg of this year's competition.
The 2027 season will bring with it a number of changes, including an increase in engine power from 400 kW to 420 kW, a five percent fuel flow increase, and a decrease in the power of the motor-generator unit-kinetic from 350 kW to 300 kW.
The modifications, says F1 , are meant to address issues related to energy management and make qualifying more flat-out. We hope they’ll make races even more interesting.

Image created using AI
By Charlotte Goldstone
19 November 2026
US shippers using road haulage are increasingly abandoning annual freight contracts in favour of shorter-term agreements, as soaring diesel prices outpace freight rate increases, according to new research from EASE Logistics.
The Ohio-based 3PL and 4PL provider’s Q3 26 Automotive Freight Index revealed a sharp shift in procurement strategies, with annual contracts falling from 80% of its automotive bids in September 2025 to just 45% a year later.
In food and beverage, the proportion dropped from 81% to 51% by August as shippers sought “greater flexibility amid volatile transport costs”.
Diesel prices exceeded $6 a gallon in September for the first time, fuel costs rising considerably faster than freight rates, which EASE reported had increased 27% year on year, compared with a 54% surge in diesel prices.
Refrigerated linehaul rates, meanwhile, were up 24% at the end of August, against a 50% increase in fuel costs.
Fuel’s share of carrier operating costs soared, from 20% in July to 28% in September, leaving operators exposed to rising expenditure before higher rates could be negotiated.
“Most companies shipping freight have recognised there is a longer-term cost impact that can’t be ignored,” said EASE chief strategy officer Ken Adamo.
Although contract pricing is beginning to catch up, with EASE’s contract cost per mile rising 6.5% between Q2 and Q3, spot rates declined 2% over the same period.
Regional disparities are also emerging, particularly in the south-east, where electric vehicle-related freight lanes into Georgia, Tennessee, and Alabama recorded average year-on-year rate growth of 35.6%, compared with 27.4% nationally.
“Due to the current industry conditions, we are advising companies to price and review Georgia, Tennessee, and Alabama lanes separately from their national network, and check them monthly rather than once a year,” said EASE director of revenue management and market intelligence Alex Perry.
Refrigerated freight is facing additional capacity pressures, with EASE citing DAT research suggesting carrier numbers are declining more rapidly in the sector, partly because of English language proficiency enforcement and other service initiatives in the southern states.
The resulting constraints could extend beyond seasonal produce movements into markets requiring refrigerated trailers for freeze protection, even as overall freight capacity eases.
And the findings echo concerns in Europe, where the IRU recently warned that record road freight rates were masking deteriorating haulier margins, again as operating costs outpace contract pricing. And shippers there are now changing contract strategies accordingly.
Rather than relying on traditional annual tenders, EASE advised shorter contract terms, regional and mid-cycle bids, and closer scrutiny of fuel surcharge mechanisms to manage volatility.
“If capacity floods back and demand stays flat, spot stays stuck and contract eventually tops out,” said Mr Adamo.
“If capacity stays disciplined and we get even a modest demand catalyst, things could get interesting quickly.”

UPS agreed to buy Smartways Logistics, a medical courier that handles urgent shipments across Australia and New Zealand. The deal would give UPS Healthcare more options for delivering medical devices, clinical trial materials and radiopharmaceuticals, which are radioactive drugs used in diagnosis and treatment.
What’s Related
UPS expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory reviews and approvals. The company did not disclose the purchase price or other terms.
Smartways has more than 350 medical couriers and serves more than 1,300 hospitals daily, according to its owner, private equity firm The Riverside Company. UPS says it plans to connect those local courier services with its global healthcare shipping and distribution business .
How Smartways handles urgent shipments
Smartways runs its urgent delivery service around the clock. For an emergency shipment headed from a city to a regional hospital, the company can assign a driver to take it directly to its destination. Its air freight service puts shipments on the next available flight and uses agreements with domestic airlines to load them last and unload them first.
Dispatchers monitor urgent shipments and can change routes if traffic or flight schedules shift. Customers can track the courier by GPS on most urgent deliveries, and Smartways says it alerts customers to disruptions before the scheduled arrival time.
Getting surgical kits back after use
Smartways also handles the return trip for loaned surgical instruments. After delivering a kit, the courier company tracks the scheduled surgery date and coordinates with the hospital’s sterile services department to collect it. This helps medical device suppliers get kits back sooner so they can send them out again.
Riverside invested in Smartways in 2021. Since then, the courier has expanded its delivery coverage across both countries and added services for life sciences companies. It also built out a system that helps hospitals, device makers, and logistics providers coordinate shipments of medical equipment.
Where Smartways fits into UPS Healthcare
UPS already offers temperature-controlled shipping and storage, along with order fulfillment for drug and medical device makers. The Smartways deal would add a local courier business set up to handle deliveries with tight deadlines. UPS did not give a timetable for combining the two companies’ services after the deal closes.
The agreement follows the October opening of UPS’s more than $80 million hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines. The hub has refrigerated and freezer storage, as well as a station where workers can replenish ice in temperature-sensitive shipments while they’re in transit. UPS said its healthcare business reached $3 billion in revenue for the third consecutive quarter in the third quarter of 2026.

2027 Alpine A290 Premiere Edition Heading to Japan in RHD, Only 100 Units on the Way
7 photos
Photo: Alpine / edited
Alpine has brought its first electric model to Japan, where prospective customers are presented with a limited availability problem. The launch specification, which is called A290 Premiere Edition, is capped at 100 examples. Nicely equipped from the outset, said B-segment electric hatchback carries a starting price of 6,490,000 yen, converting to nearly 40,600 dollars at current exchange rates.
Truth be told, Alpine 's urban dweller is expensive back home in France as well. The most affordable of the bunch is the 130-kW GT, which costs 34,670 euros in combination with the government's 4,830-euro Certificats d'Economies d'Energie bonus. Indeed, the French supermini is expensive in all configurations.
Alpine Japan's advertised price includes consumption tax, and the Premiere Edition is neatly split between two colors. Each features a front-mounted electric motor with 218 ps (215 hp) on tap, along with a 52-kWh battery pack. Alpine Japan has yet to confirm when less expensive versions will become available. For now, the well-equipped Premiere Edition will have to suffice in Japan.
Its available paint colors are called Blanc Nival and Blue Alpine Vision. Both are joined by a Noir Profond-painted roof, and both feature different brake caliper finishes. Blue cars receive blue calipers, naturally, while the white A290 Premiere Edition gets red ones. There is no such differentiation inside, where Alpine went for Deep Glue and Ever Grey Nappa leather upholstery throughout.
Customers who put money down between November 19, 2026, and March 31, 2026, receive 12 months of free Alpine Charging Card membership. Said charging card provides access to the e-Mobility Power charging network, and obviously, every kilowatt-hour consumed at those stations has to be paid by the customer.
Photo: Alpine Measuring a little over 4 meters from bumper to bumper, the angry-looking A290 Premiere Edition is a very small car. Alpine Japan lists 2,535 millimeters for the wheelbase, namely 99.8 inches in American speak. Its curb weight of 1,480 kilograms (3,263 pounds), however, is a reminder that electric vehicles are heavier than their internal combustion equivalents.
Capable of seating five, the Renault 5 E-Tech's fancier and sportier cousin is very different where it matters from the volume-oriented sibling. The suspension, chassis, and electronic controls are unique to the Alpine, which its maker developed from the outset to be the superior driving machine. Good for 300 Newton-meters (221 pound-feet) at full chatter, the A290 Premiere Edition hits 100 kph (62 mph) in 6.4 seconds.
Its high-voltage battery sits low under the floor, helping lower the center of gravity while also freeing up cabin space. Alpine Japan quotes no more than 360 kilometers (224 miles) in the WLTC test cycle, and the local division references data obtained by a French testing organization using a British-market vehicle. Only available in RHD, the Japanese model flaunts hydraulic compression stops at every corner to control suspension movement.
Brake Torque Vectoring for the Brembo performance brakes also needs highlighting, along with Michelin Pilot Sport S 5 rubber measuring 225/40 by 19 inches. Just like European models, the A290 Premiere Edition is rocking a red OV-marked button on the steering wheel. Press it, and the powertrain delivers max output for no more than 10 seconds.
A heated steering wheel, adaptive cruise control, heated front seats, rear brake support, and a 60:40 split-folding rear bench are on the menu as well. Every A290 Premiere Edition ships with a Devialet audio system that includes nine speakers, a sub, and a dedicated amp, delivering 615 watts. Said audio setup is used by the Alpine Drive Sound system to play synthetic electric soundscapes designed around its zero-emission powertrain.

source_document.body:
Porsche’s latest electric vehicle isn’t a new Taycan or Macan EV. In fact, it’s not even a full-sized car. Instead, the German automaker has teamed up with British luxury miniature car builder Hedley Studios to create an 80%-scale electric replica of one of Porsche’s most iconic racing cars, the legendary 550 Spyder.
Known as the Porsche 550 J, the pint-sized electric sports car will make its public debut at the Icons of Porsche festival in Dubai on November 21-22, celebrating 75 years of Porsche motorsport.
If Hedley Studios sounds familiar, that’s because we’ve covered the company before, back when it was known as The Little Car Company. Among its more entertaining projects was a life-sized recreation of the famous Japanese Tamiya Wild One RC dune buggy , turning a childhood remote-controlled favorite into an actual drivable electric vehicle. We’ve also covered the company’s ultra-luxurious miniature electric cars, including its stunning Bentley Blower recreation .
Now the company has turned its attention to Porsche, and the result is perhaps its most impressive miniature EV yet.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
There’s something I love about miniature electric cars, combining the fun of four-wheels with the right-sized (or pint-sized) magic of mini-mobility.
The Porsche 550 J is based on the original 550 Spyder, Porsche’s first purpose-built racing sports car, which debuted in 1953 and went on to become a motorsport legend.
Despite being scaled down to 80% of the original’s dimensions, the new electric version still seats two adults. It weighs just 350 kg (772 lb), thanks partly to its lightweight tubular steel spaceframe and hand-formed carbon fiber bodywork.
The standard version features an 8 kW (11 hp) electric motor operating on a 48V system, providing a top speed of 40 mph (65 km/h) and a range of up to 30 miles (50 km).
For those who want a bit more performance from their miniature Porsche, an optional RS Pack doubles the power to 16 kW (21 hp), increases the top speed to 50 mph (80 km/h), and extends the range to 50 miles (80 km) thanks to additional batteries. The upgrade also includes drilled disc brakes and adjustable suspension.
The attention to detail goes well beyond the exterior. The car features Brembo brakes, Bilstein suspension, Continental tires, and even a wood-rimmed Nardi steering wheel, just like the original. The classic dashboard retains its three-dial layout, though the fuel gauge has been replaced with a battery meter and the original choke lever now serves as a drive mode selector.
Even the charging port is cleverly hidden beneath the chrome fuel filler cap.
The project was developed in close collaboration with Porsche over six years, with Hedley Studios gaining access to original engineering drawings, archival materials, and historic vehicles in Porsche’s museum.
Only 250 examples will be produced, with buyers able to choose historic racing liveries or custom paint finishes, including colors matching their full-sized Porsches.
Of course, this level of craftsmanship doesn’t come cheap. Prices start at £69,500 (approximately US $91,000), before taxes and options. Orders are already open through Porsche dealers and Hedley Studios, with deliveries expected to begin in spring 2027.
That’s a lot of money for a car that’s only 80% there, but then again, this isn’t really meant to be practical transportation. It’s a collector’s piece that just happens to be electric, drivable, and capable of hitting 50 mph. When there are only 250 of these being built, the £70k price is really just the entry ticket to a special, ultra-luxury club of electric mini-Porsches.
And if you ask me, that sounds like a pretty fun combination. I don’t think I’ll ever be in the market for one of these personally, but I’d sure love to be friends with someone who is!
